**Goal:** Remediate the overnight system freeze (2026-10-18 06:51-06:52) caused by a MediaTek MT7921e WiFi firmware lockup, and prevent recurrence.

**RCA summary (from journalctl):**
- Pre-crash boot ran 15 days (Oct 3 22:40 -> Oct 18 06:52) with a degraded user session: snap.snapd-desktop-integration.snapd-desktop-integration crash-restarted 22,601 times over 2+ days ('transport endpoint is not connected' on /run/user/1000/doc, 'Failed to open display'), also exhausting inotify watches (Oct 16).
- Freeze: kernel mt7921e driver emitted repeated 'driver own failed' / 'Timeout for driver own' at 06:51:43-06:52:00, then the journal ended abruptly with NO shutdown sequence (hard hang, not clean shutdown). Machine unresponsive ~3.5h until manual power-cycle at 10:37:58.
- Post-restart: WiFi renegotiated fine (1.2 Gbit/s, -28 dBm); no persistent hardware fault.
- Ruled out: OOM (none), thermal trip (none), MCE/ECC (none), full disk (17%).

**Actions:**
1. Update linux-firmware packages (esp. linux-firmware-mediatek for MT7921) and snapd.
2. Remediate snapd-desktop-integration crash loop (snap refresh; mask if recurring).
3. Evaluate kernel panic auto-reboot (kernel.panic) / pstore for future forensic capture.

**ACs (all testable):**
- AC1: apt list --upgradable shows no outstanding linux-firmware-* upgrades; linux-firmware-mediatek at latest.
- AC2: No recurrence of snapd-desktop-integration crash loop: over 24h, no repeated 'transport endpoint is not connected' / 'Failed to open display' churn; service restart counter stays 0 in current session.
- AC3: Decision documented (applied/declined with reason) on kernel.panic/pstore mitigations.
- AC4: RCA + remediation recorded as comment on this item.
data.title: Overnight machine freeze: MT7921e firmware lockup RCA and remediation

## Goal

The herdr downtime worker dispatches at most ONE audit per idle dispatch window (active-audit single-flight, WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV) and each window requires a continuous LLM idle period (>=60s with >=2 free slots, DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS=2). Under sustained agent traffic, windows are rare, so the audit tier's per-window throughput (audit skill batch drain, AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS=5 per window) is the hard ceiling on draining the completed/in_review backlog. The audit skill's batch drain already processes multiple QUEUED items after the first dispatch, but herdr can only seed that batch with ONE dispatch per window and does not adapt its window cadence to backlog depth.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 - Depth-aware audit dispatch**: when the audit-eligible backlog (completed/in_review items without a fresh audit, per the existing staleness/recency windows) exceeds a configured threshold (e.g. QUEUE_DEPTH_BATCH_THRESHOLD), the audit tier considers dispatching MORE than one audit target per window (subject to the same idle gate, free-slot minimums and active-audit single-flight), so a deep queue drains faster within a window.
2. **AC2 - Interactive safety preserved**: no dispatch ever occurs without the existing idle-duration gate and DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS=2; the relaxed depth-aware path only raises the per-window COUNT, never the gate strictness.
3. **AC3 - No duplicate dispatch**: the existing dispatched-marker exclusion and active-audit single-flight continue to hold per item; the depth-aware path launches distinct items only.
4. **AC4 - Test coverage**: herdr unit tests assert (a) single-dispatch behaviour at shallow depth is unchanged, (b) N>1 audit dispatches when depth>=threshold, (c) the idle gate still blocks all dispatch when undersatisfied.
5. **AC5 - Full herdr test suite passes** with the change.

## Constraints

- Keep the strict idle gate for interactive protection (reserve >=1 local slot); only the per-window audit COUNT may adapt to backlog depth.
- Must not destabilize leader election/lease (5-min TTL), check-ins, pruning, fail-closed lookups, or the coordination offer path.
- The audit skill's own batch drain (AUDIT_BATCH_* in SorraAgents) remains the mechanism that processes many queued items after a dispatch; herdr only seeds the window.

## Related work

- WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV - active-audit single-flight (the constraint this item relaxes per-window, not per-item)
- WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL - downtime dispatcher leader election
- WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 - idle-gate slot requirements (AC3)
- SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (SorraAgents) - audit batch drain mode that consumes the seeded window
data.title: Herdr audit dispatch: deepen per-window batch when the in_review queue is deep

# Tests: herdr request-priority mappings & interactive dispatch

Test-first unit tests defining the herdr-side request-priority contract (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH), so implementation can proceed test-first.

## Goal
Executable specs for the two priority-mapping tables and for the interactive dispatch environment threading, in `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.test.ts` (plus the existing spawn/arg-builder tests).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Interactive mapping table:** a pure helper maps work-item `low` → `medium`, `medium` → `high`, `high` → `high`, `critical` → `high`; and maps an absent/unresolvable item (no id, lookup failure, timeout) → `high`.
- [ ] **Downtime mapping table:** a pure helper maps work-item `low` → `low`, `medium` → `medium`, `high` → `high`, `critical` → `high`; and maps an unknown/absent priority → `medium`.
- [ ] **Headless dispatch:** a test proves `spawnBackgroundPi` adds `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (already-mapped value) to the child process env, and that an unmapped/unresolvable dispatch defaults to `high`.
- [ ] **Pane arg/script contract:** a test proves the `send-to-pi.sh` argument builder forwards the request priority so the spawned pane process receives `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (the `exec env …` / `pane split --env` / `grid.py` passthrough form chosen during implementation).
- [ ] Tests reside next to the code they exercise and are initially red (new modules/arguments do not yet exist), so the implementation children can turn them green.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` (headless/arg-builder coverage) or the existing spawn test module

## Notes
- Exact tables are fixed by the parent ACs; do not relax them.
- Fail-open is required: a lookup failure must never abort a dispatch.
data.title: Tests: priority mapping & interactive dispatch
